title: Mikal Bridges' game-winning shot may be just what the Knicks guard needed - CBS Sports
description: Bridges sunk the Blazers with his second-career buzzer-beater on Saturday, and the Knicks are hoping it snaps him
body:
Bridges sunk the Blazers with his second-career buzzer-beater on Saturday, and the Knicks are hoping it snaps him out of his funk
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:19 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in New York. The Knicks sold everything but their soul to get him. He went from zero to hero over last year's championship run, then right back down to zero to start this season. Bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits. The familiar chatter was growing louder. Trade him. Or at least bench him. The Knicks entered Saturday having lost Bridges' minutes by a starter-worst five points per 100 possessions this season, per Databallr, and worse, they were +17.8 with him on the bench. He's been showing signs of life of late. He went for 18 on 8-of-12 shooting against Indiana a week ago. He put up 17 on 7-of-11 in a win over the Raptors on Tuesday. The Knicks entered Saturday having won three straight and seven of their last nine. Make that four straight and eight of 10 as the Knicks stunned the Blazers 97-96 -- with Bridges turning his ever-extreme dial from zero all the way back up to hero with the shot that just may have turned his season around. 
"Bang! Bang!"Mike Breen doesn't bring out the double-bang often, but he did it on Saturday when Bridges took an inbound pass at the top of the key and, with the Knicks down two and 3.2 seconds on the clock, dribbled left and pulled up for the second buzzer-beater of his career (both of which have come against the Blazers). 
This would've been a gut-punch loss for the Knicks, who were on the verge of fumbling a 23-point halftime lead. Instead, as it turned out, it couldn't have been scripted better. Bridges needed a moment like this.Mike Brown hasn't pulled him from the starting five, but he only played him for 17 minutes in two straight games less than two weeks ago, and Bridges' minutes, largely as a result of that stretch, are down to a career-low 26 a game, which is the same burn Landry Shamet gets. This Nov. 15 portrait of basketball depression just about summed up the state of Bridges' season at that point. 
Fast forward to Saturday night, when Madison Square Garden came alive with more than 50 franchise legends in the building for Homecoming Night, and this is what you call a vibe shift. 
"When, quote-unquote, you think he's struggling, he just keeps playing," Brown said of Bridges after Saturday's game. "He doesn't let anything impact him. ... He's not going to get too high, he's not going to get too low. He's been there and done that. So for him to have the ball in his hands at that point in the game, there's a lot of confidence not only coming from him but from his teammates and the staff."By the numbersIn the interest of not totally overreacting to one shot, let's keep some perspective on this. Bridges only had 12 points vs. Portland. The Knicks still lost his 28 minutes by six points, the worst plus-minus of the night. But he made five of his eight shots and established a confident early rhythm. 
Bridges certainly hasn't been setting the world on fire, but for the most part he's been looking more like himself after a terrible start. The Knicks are now -49 for the season in Bridges' minutes, but they were -50 over the first three games, meaning he has been a net neutral since. That's nothing to celebrate, but it's not as bad as the prevailing perception. Now look at it the other way. The Knicks are +140 without Bridges on the court this season and, while there's no denying his contribution to that number with too many nothing offensive showings, understand that nearly half of it comes from two games (-24 against the Nets on Nov. 2 and -36 against the Bucks on Nov. 11). This isn't to suggest Bridges has been anywhere close to good so far. It's just to say that small samples can look like bigger deals than they are, and generally speaking, he's been slowly coming around. Maybe he just needed one game, one shot, one moment to reroute his basketball brain back toward the space he left it in as a playoff hero. Maybe Saturday night was that moment. Like the great Don Henley said: In a New York minute, everything can change.

title: 2026 Pac-12 Championship Game: Boise State, San Diego State set for rematch - CBS Sports
description: Boise State will get a chance to avenge its loss two weeks after falling to San Diego State
body:
Boise State will get a chance to avenge its loss two weeks after falling to San Diego State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:34 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026 Pac-12 Championship matchup was set in the earliest moments of Sunday morning for half the country. San Diego State stunned No. 17 Boise State on the blue turf to punch its ticket to the conference title game.Going into Saturday, the Broncos had already secured home-field advantage in the Pac-12 Championship, but their opponent was still up in the air. The Aztecs simply needed a win over Boise State — easier said than done as three-score underdogs -- and Texas State needed a win and a San Diego State loss.The Bobcats got a win over Washington State, but the Aztecs didn't cooperate with their championship dreams. San Diego State went toe-to-toe with Boise State and kicked a game-winning field goal as time expired. Now, the Aztecs will return to Albertsons Stadium in less than two weeks to play for a conference championship.As a result, a Texas State team that pushed Boise State to the limit in a 46-45 loss last month is on the outside looking in. If this is the type of drama the revamped Pac-12 is going to provide every year, then we're all in for a treat as college football fans.
Now that the championship matchup is locked in, here is everything you need to know about each team.WATCH Pac-12 Championship: 8 p.m. Friday, Dec. 4, CBS, Paramount+ Premium)
                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about Boise StateFor most of the season, the Broncos have looked much more impressive than they did on Saturday night. Boise State lost to Oregon by seven points in Week 1 before rattling off nine straight victories.Offensively, Boise State is led by quarterback Maddux Madsen and running back Dylan Riley. Madsen took a big step forward this fall, setting a new career high in completion percentage while cutting down on interceptions. He did all that while throwing for 236.3 yards per game -- the best mark of his career. Madsen missed some time with injury earlier in the season, but backup Max Cutforth stepped in and didn't skip a beat, which is a credit to coach Spencer Danielson.
Riley has been a workhorse on the ground, and he leads the Pac-12 with 11 rushing touchdowns. He can be used in the passing game too, and Riley is up to 1,677 yards from scrimmage and 13 total touchdowns.The defense, meanwhile, hasn't been quite as strong in Boise. Since Oct. 10, the Broncos have allowed at least 31 points four times in six games. Boise State won all those games, but it's playing with fire. This unit is particularly vulnerable through the air, where it's surrendering 274.1 yards per game.Boise State entered the season as one of the favorites to reach the College Football Playoff as a Group of Six team. The Broncos can still get there, but that path is murkier following Saturday night's loss to the Aztecs. Boise State was the only Group of Six team in last week's CFP rankings, so what will the selection committee do now?

                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about San Diego StateThe Aztecs' path to the Pac-12 title game wasn't as aesthetically pleasing as the Broncos', but it was still effective. SDSU started 1-3 with losses to James Madison and Toledo. Coach Sean Lewis was facing questions about his offense -- and his tenure overall.From there, it was one step forward and one step back. The Aztecs entered Halloween with a 2-2 record in conference play. Since then, they've rattled off three straight wins against Pac-12 opponents, including Boise State. It was an impressive turnaround for a team that looked dead in the water one month earlier.While Boise State has won with offense, SDSU has won with its defense. Over the course of this three-game winning streak, the Atecas have allowed an average of 17.7 points per game. That's allowed an inconsistent offense to manufacture enough points to pick up some wins.
Cornerback Mike Lindsay has been one of the standouts on defense, and he recorded his fourth interception of the season against Boise State. In the trenches, Djibril Rahman has been a wrecking ball with 10.0 tackles for loss and five sacks.On the other side of the ball, the Aztecs have endured an unsettled quarterback position. Jayden Denegal began the season as the starter and struggled, but an injury opened the door for Stone Saunders, who has guided the offense throughout this winning streak.Boise State vs. San Diego State predictionThe Aztecs know they can go into Boise and win. The championship game comes 13 days after they upset the Broncos on the blue turf, so their confidence should be high. Having said that, it will be hard for SDSU to beat Boise State twice in Albertsons Stadium. The Broncos effectively had the game in hand before a series of baffling game-management decisions by Danielson gave the Aztecs new life. Boise State won't make those same mistakes twice, and it becomes the new Pac-12's first champion. Prediction: Boise State wins the Pac-12 Championship

        There is no wider gap between two divisions in NFL history than the 2026 NFC North and the 2026 NFC South.The NFC North is a combined 27-10 this season, which is on pace to be the best mark by a division since the 1970 merger. If the playoffs started today, the NFC North would be the first division to have four playoff teams since 1998, when there were only three divisions per conference. Yes, the group is that good.The NFC South, meanwhile, is a combined 13-24. That is on pace to be the second-worst mark since the merger. (Take a bow, 2008 NFC West). Currently, the Panthers lead this woebegone division at 4-5. According to CBS Sports forecasting and projections, not a single team from the division is on pace to hit even eight wins. Compare that to the NFC North, where all four teams are projected to hit at least nine; the Packers are barely short of making it so all teams are projected to hit 10 wins.Yes, the NFC South is that bad.Whether collectively good or collectively bad, they share one thing in common: extremely competitive. And that's what matters when looking at the Week 11 games that will most impact the playoff races.

The Ravens' season is all but over after a loss to the previously winless Chargers, but the Panthers are still right in the thick of things as the NFC South leaders. It might not be pretty, but "pretty" and "NFC South" were never going to match, anyway. Plus, Carolina needs to keep stacking wins, especially against struggling opponents.

        Trevor Lawrence has spent the past 17 regular-season games building an MVP résumé. On Sunday against the Giants (4:25 p.m., CBS and live streaming on Paramount+), the Jaguars quarterback gets another opportunity to show why his candidacy deserves more attention.Yes, it may be weird to read the words "NFL MVP candidate" next to the Jaguars' quarterback, which is understandable. Jacksonville is the only current franchise in the league that has never had a player receive a first-place MVP vote. However, Lawrence is performing like an MVP-caliber quarterback for a Jaguars team whose 7-2 record is tied for the next-best record in the NFL, behind only the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers and the 8-1 Buffalo Bills. It's just the third time in franchise history the Jaguars have started 7-2 or better through their first nine games, and the first time since 1999, according to Stathead. Among qualified quarterbacks, Lawrence ranks top-five in the league in pass yards per attempt, passing touchdowns, passer rating, success rate and EPA (expected points added) per dropback, plus a top-10 finish in touchdown-to-interception ratio and completion percentage, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Trevor Lawrence 2026 season, NFL ranksNFL ranksCompletion percentage66.3%9thSuccess rate50.4%5thPass yards per attempt8.92ndPass TD21T-3rdTD-INT21-56thPasser Rating112.83rdExpected points added (EPA) per dropback0.252ndThat's why DraftKings Sportsbook is giving him the fourth-best odds (+550) to take home the NFL MVP hardware entering Week 11. The only three players with better odds are Joe Burrow (-125), Josh Allen (+370), and Brock Purdy (+450). However, Lawrence is also racking up eye-popping numbers in an offense without any other established NFL stars, unlike the three quarterbacks ahead of him. Burrow has Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at wide receiver, plus four-time Pro Bowler Orlando Brown Jr. at left tackle. Allen has 2025 NFL rushing champion James Cook at running back and five-time Pro Bowler Dion Dawkins at left tackle. Purdy has 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey at running back, plus George Kittle and Trent Williams. Close your eyes and think. Who is the most accomplished Jacksonville offensive player outside of Lawrence? Running back Bhayshul Tuten is in just his second NFL season and his first as a lead back. No. 1 wide receiver Parker Washington, a 2023 sixth-round pick, is in his fourth NFL season and has never recorded a 1,000-yard receiving season -- he is well on pace to do so for the first time in 2026 with 645 yards receiving in the first 9 games of the year, which ranks 16th in the league. None of his offensive linemen have ever earned a Pro Bowl selection. Lawrence is uplifting a cast of solid, budding young talent and producing at an elite level similar to, or better than in some metrics, the other quarterbacks up for NFL MVP through 10 weeks. This first-half performance in 2026 isn't a fluke either. Once Lawrence adjusted to coach Liam Coen's scheme halfway through 2025, their first season together, he led the entire NFL in total touchdowns with 24 across the last eight games of the 2025 regular season, a span in which Jacksonville went a perfect 8-0 to finish 13-4 and win the AFC South. Lawrence's 38 total touchdowns ranked as the third-most in football last season behind only the league's last two MVP winners: Matthew Stafford (46) and Josh Allen (39). That's how he finished fifth in 2025 NFL MVP voting, behind only Stafford, Drake Maye, Allen and McCaffrey last season. Across the final six games of the 2025 season, Lawrence produced a ridiculous 19 total touchdowns to just one turnover. That feat made him just the third player in NFL history to record 19-plus total touchdowns and one or fewer turnovers in the final six games of a season. The other two players to do so are 2019 Drew Brees (20 total touchdowns to one turnover) and 2020 NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers (21 total touchdowns to one turnover). Combining the second half of last season and the first half of this season, Lawrence has 15 wins and 45 total touchdowns in his last 17 regular-season games. title: College football grades: Texas earns 'A', Indiana gets 'D' on Week 12 report card - CBS Sports
description: A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 12 action
body:
A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 12 action
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:37 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When Texas quarterback Arch Manning takes care of the football and keeps the Longhorns ahead of the chains, it does wonders for his team's championship viability. In a 45-3 Week 12 throttling of Arkansas, the fourth-year quarterback completed 21 of 25 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns while registering his third-best quarterback rating of the season.The easy win produced a collective exhale around Austin, as it basically locked up Texas' spot in the College Football Playoff. Even if the Longhorns take a stunning road loss against rival Texas A&M this week, they will likely be in the CFP at 9-3. But if Manning plays as he did against the Razorbacks, Texas should crush the vulnerable Aggies.To be sure, the Longhorns' defense bowed up when Arkansas got into Texas territory and repeatedly came up with stops. That was part of the victory equation. But everything was made simpler for Texas because the Longhorns didn't turn the football over. It was the first time since a Week 3 win over UTSA that Texas played 60 minutes of turnover-free football. Thus, the Longhorns get an 'A' on this week's report card.We are handing out grades evaluating every team that started or ended the day with national championship odds of +3000 or better. 
2026 national championship odds are listed below, courtesy of DraftKings. Teams listed in order of their College Football Playoff ranking. 
        
            
                Week 12 CFB Overreactions: Ohio State will miss the CFP, but it is not nation's most disappointing team
                
                    Brandon Marcello                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 GeorgiaGrade: AResult: 34-6 win vs. South CarolinaTitle odds: +200South Carolina coach Shane Beamer essentially declared it a moral victory during his halftime interview with ESPN, when Georgia led just 10-6. Then came the second half. The Bulldogs outscored the Gamecocks 24-0 the rest of the way by doubling up the Gamecocks in time of possession while earning a fourth straight 3+ possession win over SEC competition. Georgia isn't just winning. It is throttling SEC competition in a way that suggests it's a cut above the rest of the sport.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 UtahGrade: B+Result: 38-17 win at TCUTitle odds: +2800A TCU team that looked dead offensively in the first half rallied from a 17-0 deficit to tie the game in the fourth quarter. But the Utes rattled off 17 unanswered in the final six minutes to remain the only unbeaten FBS team. Star quarterback Devon Dampier came alive down the stretch and clinched the game with an 85-yard touchdown pass and a 10-yard touchdown run. The Heisman candidate totaled four touchdowns. Overall, the start and finish were great, while the middle stretch exposed some vulnerabilities in a defense that will need to be better if the Utes are going to make a deep playoff run.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 AlabamaGrade: BResult: 47-0 win vs. ChattanoogaTitle odds: +600Ahead of next week's Iron Bowl showdown with Auburn and a potential CFP run, getting out of a glorified scrimmage vs. an FCS opponent without injury concerns would have been nice. But left guard Mal Waldrep left the game with an injury in the first half and didn't return. Defensive back Chuck McDonald III also exited in the first half. Bama was smart to rest starting quarterback Keelon Russell. There wasn't much real insight to gain from a meaningless game that will serve as a weight on Alabama's resume at a time when the Crimson Tide are jockeying for a first-round bye.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 UCLAGrade: C-Result: 18-16 (OT) loss at MichiganTitle odds: +12000UCLA's defense did its job, as Michigan's woeful offense continued to struggle. But after entering tied for first nationally with a +16 turnover margin, the Bruins coughed it up three times and only got one takeaway. A fumble by quarterback Ty Dieffenbach at the end of the third quarter led directly to Michigan's only touchdown of the game. The Bruins couldn't stack explosive plays on offense and struggled to stay ahead of the chains from down to down. An injury to Dieffenbach in overtime could prove especially problematic moving forward.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 TexasGrade: AResult: 45-3 win vs. ArkansasTitle odds: +650Texas' drama-free win over Arkansas offered a vision for what UT can be when things are clicking. Arch Manning played efficient and turnover-free football, and the defense held Arkansas out of the end zone. The Razorbacks often moved the football, but they never finished drives. This result -- combined with UCLA's loss and Alabama's unofficial bye week against an FCS team -- will probably put Texas into the top four of the new CFP Rankings.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Notre DameGrade: B-Result: 24-3 win vs. SMUTitle odds: +400Notre Dame's defense came up with three huge red-zone stops, stifling an SMU offense that can be dangerous. It wasn't always pretty, but this was a pass/fail assignment for the Fighting Irish, who simply need to survive and advance to get within one win of being a playoff lock at 11-1. No style points were required, which is a good thing since Notre Dame didn't score for the game's final 26+ minutes.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 MiamiGrade: C+Result: 28-20 win vs. Virginia TechTitle odds: +1300The final score belies the fact that Miami mostly dominated this game. Virginia Tech started with a splash but lost its way offensively over the final three quarters as the Hurricanes began to dominate. On a night when Miami's vaunted offense didn't have its best stuff amid the continued absence of star receiver Malachi Toney, the defense stepped up. But it's hard to ignore how this team's national title odds are slipping.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 IndianaGrade: DResult: 27-24 (OT) loss at WashingtonTitle odds: +1900CFP Selection Committee chair Hunter Yurachek highlighted Indiana's improved offense(??) while justifying the Hoosiers' one-spot rise in the rankings last week. He suggested that if the unit continued to play well, it would do "nothing but help them in the eyes of the committee." Well, not only did Indiana limp to a 2-for-15 mark on third downs against Washington while reigniting a quarterback controversy by pulling Grant Wilson, but it also dealt with uncharacteristic defensive lapses. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 TennesseeGrade: B+Result: 27-13 win vs. LSUTitle odds: +2000Tennessee's defense might be the single most impactful offense/defensive unit for any top-10 team. The Volunteers frustrated LSU all game by amassing 13 tackles for loss, including eight sacks, while bringing themselves to the doorstep of a CFP bid. The passing game remains problematic, but the defense is absolutely elite. First-year coordinator Jim Knowles may go down as the best coordinator hire of the 2026 season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 Wake ForestGrade: A-Result: 50-29 win vs. Georgia TechTitle odds: +2200Wake Forest has gone flying up the odds sheet over the past couple of weeks while continuing to pile up points at a gaudy clip. The Demon Deacons led Georgia Tech 50-15 at one point while amassing 607 total yards. After another 21-point victory, Wake Forest tops the nation with a +310 point margin.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 OregonGrade: AResult: 45-7 win at Michigan StateTitle odds: +2400An Oregon team that was left for dead following a 4-3 start is now very much alive to reach the Big Ten Championship Game and College Football Playoff after an authoritative beatdown of Michigan State and some favorable results elsewhere in the Big Ten. The Ducks pulled away from Michigan State with a balanced offensive attack and a defense that forced four three-and-outs.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 14 Ohio StateGrade: DResult: 31-28 loss at NebraskaTitle odds: N/AOhio State became the first ranked team to lose against Nebraska since 2016 as the Buckeyes floundered defensively again. Nebraska wrecked the Buckeyes on third downs as Ohio State notched just one sack on Anthony Colandrea, who wreaked havoc as a runner. Heisman candidate Jeremiah Smith's 165 receiving yards and two touchdowns were a bright spot. But this loss made it official that the only potentially meaningful hardware in Ohio State's future will be for Smith's individual achievements.

title: Tom Fornelli's CFP Vibe Check: Big Ten bloodbath leaves league on brink - CBS Sports
description: The Big 12 and ACC strengthened their playoff positions, Iowa gained new life, and UCLA faces major questions aft
body:
The Big 12 and ACC strengthened their playoff positions, Iowa gained new life, and UCLA faces major questions after losing its first game and another starting quarterback
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:04 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Every week, the CFP Vibe Check tries to put its finger on where things stand in the College Football Playoff race without overreacting to what it just saw, but also probably overreacting to everything it just saw. The Big Ten may go from winning three straight national titles to being a one-bid league in the blink of an eye. There is no way to describe how Week 12 went for the Big Ten other than an absolute bloodbath from a College Football Playoff perspective.Things started well enough Friday night with Oregon posting the kind of blowout win it needs to make a case for an at-large, beating Michigan State 45-7, but that was the end of Big Ten success. No. 8 Indiana lost to Washington 27-24 in overtime. No. 14 Ohio State lost to Nebraska 31-28, ending Nebraska's 31-game losing streak against ranked teams. And what may prove to be the biggest blow of all: No. 4 UCLA not only suffered its first loss of the season, falling to Michigan 18-16 in triple overtime, but also lost its quarterback, Ty Dieffenbach, to injury during overtime.Dieffenbach had to be carted off the field. While we don't know the severity of the injury, it's hard to imagine he'll be available to play next week against USC. And remember, Dieffenbach was already the team's backup QB. Nico Iamaleava, UCLA's original starter, was lost for the season earlier this year. Now the Bruins will be relying on Nico's younger brother, Madden Iamaleava, to save their season.
And as if all those results weren't bad enough on their own, they came on the same weekend the Big 12 handled its business. Every single ranked team in the Big 12 was on the road this week, and every single one of them won their game. They weren't all pretty, as No. 10 BYU needed triple-overtime to take down Kansas, and No. 2 Utah found itself tied with a TCU team starting its backup QB in the fourth quarter before pulling away to win by 21, but they all won in the end.So when the sun rises Sunday morning, the Big 12 will be sitting pretty while the Big Ten dreads what could come Tuesday night.I'll get to my complete projection for this week's rankings at the end of the column, but there is a strong chance the Big 12 could have three teams ranked ahead of the highest-ranked Big Ten team on Tuesday night. UCLA and Indiana will be lucky to stay in the top 10, while BYU and Texas Tech are poised to benefit from their fall. 
And it's not just the Big 12 causing problems. The Big Ten will probably be ranked behind two ACC teams as well. Miami didn't look great in a win over Virginia Tech, but it won and improved to 10-1. Wake Forest dominated another team, beating Georgia Tech 50-29. It's 10-1 and likely to leapfrog both UCLA and Indiana.That "1" in B1G may very well represent how many teams the league gets into the field.
        
            
                College football winners, losers: Luck runs out for Indiana, Oregon rounding into form
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
There was one B1G winner, thoughThe irony of the Big Ten's downfall in Week 12 is that there may not have been a bigger winner in the playoff picture than the No. 15 Iowa Hawkeyes this weekend. Sure, the Big 12 and ACC saw their odds of getting multiple teams skyrocket, but Iowa's chances of getting into the field increased dramatically too.
While everybody else with a chance in the Big Ten was losing, Iowa went on the road and beat Illinois 34-17. The Hawkeyes began the week ranked behind Oregon and Ohio State because they lost at home to Ohio State, and Ohio State lost at home to Oregon, and that's how the CFP's pod system works. The fact that Iowa had fewer losses was meaningless, especially when they lacked a marquee win.They still don't have a marquee win, but with Ohio State out of the way, there's a chance they'll jump Oregon, even if it's not likely. My suspicion is that, when it comes to their common opponents, the committee will value Oregon's win over Ohio State (which Iowa lost to) more than Iowa's win over Illinois (which Oregon lost to).Still, the Hawkeyes may not need the committee at all. Saturday's chaos in the Big Ten opened up a viable pathway for the Hawkeyes to Indianapolis. If Iowa beats Nebraska on Black Friday -- it has won 10 of the last 11 meetings -- the Hawkeyes have a real chance of reaching the conference title game, and could clinch a berth with a win there.
Last Tuesday, most Iowa fans thought they were dead in the water, but there's new life in Iowa City.It seems there are three open spotsWhile oddsmakers don't know everything, it's worth noting that DraftKings is no longer even listing odds to make the CFP for Georgia, Alabama or Notre Dame. They also give Utah, Miami, Texas, Tennessee and Wake Forest at least a 90% chance of making the field based on implied odds.That's eight spots spoken for, which leaves three open for Power Four at-larges. Those spots will likely go to BYU, Indiana, Oregon, Texas Tech, UCLA or Iowa. 
Will UCLA get the Florida State treatment?We all remember what happened to Florida State in 2023. The Seminoles finished the season 13-0 despite losing starting QB Jordan Travis to an injury against North Alabama. Even though the Seminoles beat Florida in Gainesville without Travis, and then beat Louisville in the ACC Championship without him, they were left out of the four-team CFP for a 12-1 Alabama because of the Travis injury.Well, UCLA lost to Michigan today, and while the Bruins could withstand one loss, I'm not as confident they can withstand the loss of Ty Dieffenbach.It's hard to imagine the committee giving UCLA an at-large if it loses to USC next week. They'd be 10-2, and their best win would be an Oregon team that had just lost its starting QB that turned the ball over seven times. They would have no other wins against a ranked opponent. That resume and the Dieffenbach injury would probably be enough of an excuse for the committee to choose anybody else with a reasonable case over the Bruins.
Even if UCLA somehow figures out a way to beat USC next week, I'm not entirely sure the committee will give them a spot if they're down to Madden Iamaleava. So my advice to UCLA is this: I don't care what's wrong with Dieffenbach. Lie about it. Tell everybody who will listen that you fully expect him to be healthy for the start of the playoff.Boise State may have thrown a playoff berth awayBoise State led San Diego State 20-13 before the Aztecs mounted a late drive to get a touchdown. Jaylon Hawkins found Stone Saunders for a 39-yard touchdown to make it 20-19 with 1:51 to play, but the Aztecs' decision to go for two didn't pay off. They then failed to recover the onside kick, and it looked as though Boise would escape with the win and with a firm grasp of the Group of Six playoff spot.
Then Boise decided to make things interesting.After handing the ball off on first and second down, forcing San Diego State to burn its final two timeouts, Boise decided to drop back and throw on third down. There was 1:36 left in the game. Maddux Madsen's pass to Keawe Brown was complete along the sideline, where Browne went out of bounds to stop the clock. Now facing a fourth-and-3 at the SDSU 45, having stopped the clock, Boise decided to go for it instead of punting. Madsen lost a yard on a draw to turn the ball over on downs.The Aztecs took over at the SDSU 46, drove 30 yards, and then sent Cooper DiLeva out to kick the game-winning 42-yard field goal.While I can understand the decision to go for it on fourth down, I'll never understand why Boise dropped back to pass on third down. Hand it off. Let another 40 seconds run off the clock. Then you either punt, or if you gained enough yardage, go for it on fourth down. Whatever you choose, you're leaving San Diego State with a lot less time to get into field goal range.
But that's not what Boise did, and now we don't know for sure whether the Broncos will be the highest-ranked G6 team this week. I think there's a decent chance they still will be, seeing as how they were No. 17 this week and no other G6 team was ranked, but at best the Broncos erased all their margin for error with a baffling decision.Rest in CFPeaceEach week for the rest of the season, we shall recognize the schools who saw their playoff hopes die over the weekendKentuckyMemphisNorth TexasOhio StateWeek 13 vibe shiftersA look ahead to the five games on next week's slate most likely to impact the playoff race

title: Broncos Ring of Fame linebacker and Hall of Fame broadcaster Tom Jackson dies at 75 - CBS Sports
description: Jackson spent his entire career with the Broncos

Jackson spent his entire career with the Broncos

    10:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
Denver Broncos legend and Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson has died at the age of 75, the team announced on Sunday. No cause of death was reported.
Jackson was a major piece of the "Orange Crush" defense, playing for the team from 1973 to 1986. He was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of the 1973 NFL Draft and spent his entire career in Denver.The three-time Pro Bowler played in 191 regular season games, with 177 starts, along with 10 playoff games. He also has two Super Bowl appearances, starting in the 1977 championship game, the Broncos first trip to the big game, and 1986. His 20 interceptions are tied for the most by a linebacker in team history and his seven picks in the 1976 season are the most by a linebacker in a single season in Broncos history. The first-team All-Pro has a career 40.0 sacks and three touchdowns. Jackson's excellence throughout his 14 years on the team made him a fan favorite and put him in the Broncos Ring of Fame in 1992. After he retired, he stayed in the football world as a broadcaster. He was given the Pete Rozelle Award for broadcasting by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015.

        Titans edge defender Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday night in his hometown of Tampa, Fla., and remained hospitalized, the team announced via a statement.The Tampa Police Department provided preliminary information on the crash, which happened at around 8:45 a.m. on N. MacDill Ave.Harrell, a Tampa native, was riding as a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento rideshare when "he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion," according to police. The rideshare driver, a man in his mid-30s, reportedly swerved, striking a second car before crashing into a utility pole. Upon impact, police say Harrell was thrown forward, striking the windshield and losing consciousness. 
"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the statement said. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information. At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."Harrell, 24, tore his ACL in August and has been on injured reserve ever since, which explains his absence from the team. The Titans visit the Cowboys on Sunday.
A seventh-round pick out of Michigan in 2024, Harrell has spent his entire NFL career with the Titans. He appeared in all 17 games in both 2024 and 2025, contributing on defense and special teams. He had 4.5 sacks last season as well. He is the son of former Lions and Chiefs linebacker James Harrell.

title: Week 12 CFB Overreactions: Ohio State will miss the CFP, but it is not nation's most disappointing team - CBS Sports
description: Plus, Wake Forest makes a convincing playoff push, Jeremiah Smith locks up the Heisman Trophy and a chaotic weeke
body:
Plus, Wake Forest makes a convincing playoff push, Jeremiah Smith locks up the Heisman Trophy and a chaotic weekend reshapes the postseason race
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 22, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:08 am ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Dare I say we haven't had a single bad week of college football this season?This week didn't feature a single game featuring two teams ranked in the AP poll, and yet three of the top 15 teams in the College Football Playoff rankings lost to unranked opponents, including Indiana and previously unbeaten UCLA, which each lost overtime games within minutes of each other. We head into the final week with one dominant program atop the rankings (Georgia), an undefeated Utah out of the Big 12 and a mess of contenders below them who could win or lose any week against any opponent. The proof is in the schedule. Half of the CFP's Top 10 teams have lost to at least one unranked opponent this season. No. 5 Texas (9-2), which leads the country with five ranked wins, lost twice to teams who were unranked at the time. So, for those who believe a 24-team playoff won't produce a massive upset or two in 2027 and beyond, may I share with you the 24 teams that would have been in the field last week -- most of them losers to unranked teams at some point this season.
This isn't the college football landscape of two or three years ago. The game has changed. Teams are not as deep, and every program is one key injury away from humility.Let's dig deeper into a few instant, reactionary takes on the penultimate week of the 2026 season:The nation's two best teams are in the SECTexas needs help with tiebreakers to play Georgia in the SEC Championship Game, but might we see the two face off in the CFP?
Most of the country's top-tier teams have been shaky over the last few weeks, but not Georgia or Texas. Georgia is steamrolling SEC teams, winning seven of its nine by at least 19 points on its way to clinching a sixth straight trip to the SEC Championship Game. Meanwhile, Texas is on a five-game winning streak and has won a nation-leading five games against AP-ranked foes.Undefeated UCLA fell to a .500 Michigan squad and suffered another quarterback injury, forcing the No. 4 Bruins to play their third-string quarterback in overtime. No. 2 Utah was tied with five minutes remaining against unranked TCU. No. 8 Indiana lost at Washington. No. 10 BYU needed overtime to defeat Kansas.Find two teams with better resumes. You can't. The Bulldogs and Longhorns are the two best teams in the country heading into the final week of the regular season.
That might change if/when Miami gets superstar receiver Malachi Toney back on the field for the ACC Championship Game, but for now, I'd take Georgia or Texas over any team in the CFP top 10.BYU isn't a playoff teamBYU is riding a win against Notre Dame into the playoff, but should it be in that position following subpar showings over the last several weeks?No. 10 BYU squeezed out a 31-29 victory in triple overtime at four-win Kansas on Saturday, the latest lackluster performance by the Cougars, who just haven't seemed like themselves since beating then-No. 2 Notre Dame on Oct. 17. BYU is 2-2 in its last four, with losses at UCF and at rival Utah, which is arguably a top-four team in the country, but that doesn't discount the shakiness.
On Saturday, the Cougars led Kansas by 10 points in the second half, allowed Kansas to rally and tie, then badly missed a 37-yard field goal for the win with three seconds remaining in regulation.Kansas made some questionable play calls in overtime, too, to help the Cougs.BYU should be jumped by Wake Forest and Texas Tech in the playoff rankings. I'm also open to entertaining an argument for Oregon, which is rolling since the change at offensive coordinator.Wake Forest is spicyQuestion the schedule, downplay the offense and ignore No. 11 Wake Forest all you want, but the Demon Deacons are not going away.
The Deacs defeated Georgia Tech 50-29 in a game that was never really that close, as its blazing offense continues to overwhelm the ACC. They have outscored their last five opponents 181-7 in the first half, the largest point differential over five games since Alabama in 2018. Their last seven games have been decided by at least three touchdowns.Quarterback Gio Lopez scored four more times Saturday, bringing his total to 31 scores with only one turnover this season. Why aren't we seeing him on more national awards lists?Lock the Deacs in the playoff.Go ahead and gift-wrap the Heisman TrophyMatt Rhule just pulled off the biggest win of his career, ending Nebraska's 10-year drought without a ranked win, and his first words Saturday were about a player not on his roster.
"Jeremiah Smith, give him the Heisman," Rhule said on the FOX broadcast. "I mean, we doubled him, but these kids won the game today."Smith was incredible again, catching six passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns, but No. 14 Ohio State lost for the third time in four games and was finally eliminated from the playoff hunt in the 31-28 loss. The junior's record-breaking season now stands at 1,482 receiving yards and 17 touchdowns. Argue all you want about wins and losses, but it's clear who the best player on the field is every time Ohio State plays. At this point, we might as well slap Scarlet and Gray wrapping paper on the trophy and put Jeremiah on the gift label. Challenger Darian Mensah is not what he once was with a healthy Malachi Toney at receiver, and he failed to throw a touchdown for the first time in 28 games and was picked off twice in a 28-20 win against Virginia Tech.
Anyone arguing that a player other than Smith should win the trophy for the sport's most outstanding player is doing so just to be different.The most disappointing team is …Kiffin and LSU have been stuck on six wins for weeks now.  
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Ohio State might fall out of the top 25 today for the first time in 15 years, but as disappointing as that is in Columbus, the Buckeyes are not the most disappointing team in the country.That honor belongs to Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers, who dominated the headlines since the former Ole Miss coach betrayed the Rebels in December, stormed Baton Rouge, signed the nation's No. 1 transfer class and subsequently face-planted in the bayou.
What does five losses cost these days? If you're LSU, it's roughly $107 million total in buyout money to fire Brian Kelly, a new contract for Kiffin and his assistants, and NIL contracts for one of the most expensive rosters in the country.LSU's 27-13 loss at Tennessee assured the Tigers will finish the season 0-for against ranked opponents under the first-year coach, who is now 1-10 all-time as a head coach on the road against top-10 teams. His last win against a top-10 team on the road was in 2011, during that fall fling in Tennessee before he bolted Knoxville for USC.On Saturday, Kiffin also became only the fourth LSU coach since 1933 to lose five games in his debut season.
"But I'm not as concerned if it were, OK, well, we've got some really bad evals of who we're picking on our roster," Kiffin told reporters after falling to 6-5. "So we just gotta, obviously, win next week (at Arkansas). And then in the offseason we've gotta learn how to finish better and coach better, so we do better in those situations."After the off-field drama surrounding Kiffin and the in-season legal battles over professional players on the roster -- which nearly led to LSU's expulsion from the SEC -- this year was truly an embarrassment of riches for the Tigers.Iowa is a playoff teamIowa ought to be on the brink of making its debut in the College Football Playoff, standing just a single victory away.The Hawkeyes (9-2) have won four straight -- all by double digits -- and a win against Nebraska on Black Friday should put them in the field. That's if the CFP selection committee is paying attention. The Hawkeyes entered last week 15th in their rankings and need to move up four spots to clinch a spot in two weeks. Three teams above them lost Saturday.Here's the good news: three of the five remaining scenarios for the Big Ten Championship game involve Iowa, so it might get another chance to impress the committee."I swear to God, I could care less about those guys," veteran Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said after the game. "They're gonna do what they want to do and I really don't care."
